newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close flat, off day's high.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close flat, off day's high.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed marginally higher on Wednesday as short covering by speculators wiped out early gains made on institutional buying, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 1.30 points higher at 669.07.
Brokers said the re-emergence of foreign institutional investors coupled with active buying by domestic financial institutions had overheated the market.
"In short term the market was in an over-bought condition and I feel that it should witness some correction before staging another rally," said Ajit Sial of brokers Sial and Company.
Traders said the institutional buying was fuelled by the government's move to drop a proposal for the issue of non-voting shares.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told parliament on Monday that the government would not press an earlier move to amend the law to allow firms to issue non-voting shares.
Reliance Industries, after touching a peak of 198.80, closed 1.30 rupees lower at 193.35 on profit-taking by speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India gained 0.20 rupee to 218.55.
